blocks.title: Interval projection
blocks.body: For real numbers \(a\leq b\), let \(\Pi_{[a,b]}:\mathbb R\to [a,b]\) be the interval projection \(\Pi_{[a,b]}(z)=\min\{b,\max\{a,z\}\}\).

blocks.title: I.i.d. observed sampling
blocks.body: For each observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), let \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) denote the observed triple for unit \(i\). The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(\mathbb P\).

blocks.title: Consistency of outcomes
blocks.body:
The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Conditional exchangeability
blocks.body:
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the potential outcome \(Y(a)\) is conditionally independent of treatment given covariates:
\[
Y(a)\perp A\mid X .
\]

blocks.title: Fixed overlap
blocks.body:
Let \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be the finite covariate alphabet. For every observed law \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with covariate-cell mass \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the treatment propensity \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon\leq \pi_x \leq 1-\epsilon ,
\]
where \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) is the fixed overlap constant.

blocks.title: Observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\)
blocks.body:
For a full-data law \(P\), its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) is the law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) defined by
\[
\operatorname{Obs}(P)\{(x,a,y)\}
=
P(X=x,A=a,Y=y),
\qquad
(x,a,y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2.
\]

blocks.title: Observed-law class \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\)
blocks.body:
Under \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let
\[
\Delta_d=\left\{p\in[0,1]^d:\sum_{x=1}^d p_x=1\right\}.
\]
The class \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) consists of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there exist \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), propensities \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and means \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) such that, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
q_{a1,x}
=
p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},
\qquad
q_{a0,x}
=
p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where
\[
q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y).
\]
For each cell \(x\), write
\[
q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x}).
\]
The support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells, and on any null cell the parameters may be chosen arbitrarily within the displayed ranges.

blocks.title: Observed-law optimal value \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\)
blocks.body:
For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), the observed-law optimal-regression functional is
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q)
:=
\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}.
\]
This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

blocks.title: Minimax risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
blocks.body:
The fixed-sample minimax squared risk is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\inf_{\widehat V}
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P}
\left[
\left\{
\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P)
\right\}^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable maps
\[
\widehat V:\bigl([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\bigr)^n\to\mathbb R.
\]

blocks.title: Full-data causal class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\)
Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
blocks.body:
The four-cell overlap cone is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\},
\]
where, for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u).
\]

blocks.title: Global extension \(g_{a,\epsilon}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon\)
blocks.body:
For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define the overlap-stabilized arm contribution
\[
g_{a,\epsilon}(u)
:=
\frac{s(u)u_{a1}}{\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}},
\qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
and the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution
\[
\bar f_\epsilon(u)
:=
\max_{a\in\{0,1\}} g_{a,\epsilon}(u).
\]
At the origin,
\[
g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=0,
\qquad
\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0.
\]

blocks.title: Oracle value \(V^\star(P)\)
blocks.body:
For a full-data law \(P\), the full-data causal optimal-treatment value is
\[
V^\star(P)
=
E_P\!\left[
\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}
E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}
\right].
\]

blocks.title: Identification and completion
blocks.body:
Let \(d\ge 2\), let \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Cell overlap.)} For every \(x\in[d]\), the four-vector \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) belongs to the overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) of \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}.
\item \textbf{(Observed value.)} The observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d \bar f_\epsilon(q_x).
\]
\item \textbf{(Global extension bounds.)} For every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\), the global extension of \cref{obj:def:global-extension} satisfies
\[
0\le \bar f_\epsilon(u)\le s(u).
\]
\item \textbf{(Global Lipschitz property.)} For every \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\),
\[
\left|\bar f_\epsilon(u)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le (1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}\left|u_{\jmath}-v_{\jmath}\right|.
\]
\item \textbf{(Completion.)} There exists a full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class} whose observed margin satisfies \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)=\mathbb P\). The completion is consistent and conditionally exchangeable, treatment is independent of the joint potential-outcome vector given \(X\), and the two potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables given \(X\).
\item \textbf{(Observed margins.)} For every full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) of \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Causal value identification
blocks.body:
Let \(d\ge 2\), let \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(P\) be a full-data law satisfying \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Then the full-data oracle value in \cref{obj:def:oracle-value} agrees with the observed-law optimal-regression value in \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} evaluated at the observed margin in \cref{obj:def:observed-margin}:
\[
V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}.
\]

blocks.title: Empirical-ratio estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\)
blocks.body:
For \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define the empirical counts
\[
\overline N_x
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x\},
\qquad
\overline N_{ax}
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\},
\]
and
\[
\overline S_{ax}
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}.
\]
Set
\[
\widehat p_x=\frac{\overline N_x}{n},
\qquad
\widehat\mu_{ax}=\frac{\overline S_{ax}}{\overline N_{ax}},
\]
with the convention \(0/0=0\). The empirical-ratio optimal-value estimator is
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}
=
\sum_{x=1}^d \widehat p_x \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\widehat\mu_{ax}.
\]

blocks.title: Treatment-outcome coordinate set
blocks.body:
The treatment-outcome coordinate set \(\mathcal J\) is
\[
\mathcal J:=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}.
\]
A coordinate index is denoted by \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

blocks.title: Jackson polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\)
blocks.body:
For an integer \(K_d\ge 2\), define the order-four Jackson kernel on \([-\pi,\pi]\) by
\[
J_{K_d}(t)
=
c_{K_d}
\left\{
\frac{\sin(K_dt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}
\right\}^{4},
\]
with removable values filled continuously and normalizing constant \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that
\[
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1.
\]
For a rectangle
\[
Q_x
=
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}],
\]
define its coordinate centers and radii by
\[
b_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
The associated tensor polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) is defined by the even product convolution
\[
P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}
\bar f_\epsilon\{b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t)\}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt.
\]

blocks.title: Jackson-factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\)
blocks.body:
The inputs are \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the alphabet size \(d\), and tuning constants \(D_0\), \(\kappa\), and \(H_0\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the logarithmic scale, Poissonized scale, and polynomial degree by
\[
L_d=\log(ed),
\qquad
m=\frac n8,
\qquad
K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor \kappa L_d\rfloor\}.
\]

\item If \(d<D_0\), output
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}.
\]
If \(d\ge D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), output
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\frac12.
\]

\item In the remaining case, draw
\[
M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4).
\]
On the event \(M>n\), set
\[
\widetilde V=0.
\]

\item On the event \(M\le n\), draw independent marks
\[
B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,M.
\]
For each \(x\in[d]\) and coordinate \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), define pilot and evaluation counts
\[
N'_{\jmath,x}
=
\sum_{i=1}^M B_i\,\mathbf 1\{O_i\text{ belongs to coordinate }\jmath\text{ in cell }x\},
\]
and
\[
N_{\jmath,x}
=
\sum_{i=1}^M (1-B_i)\,\mathbf 1\{O_i\text{ belongs to coordinate }\jmath\text{ in cell }x\}.
\]

\item Define pilot frequencies and rectangle half-widths by
\[
c_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m},
\qquad
h_{\jmath,x}
=
H_0
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{c_{\jmath,x}L_d}{m}}
+
\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
\ell_{\jmath,x}
=
\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\},
\qquad
u_{\jmath,x}
=
c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x},
\]
and
\[
Q_x
=
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}].
\]
Let \(b_x\) and \(r_x\) denote the vector of coordinate centers and coordinate radii of \(Q_x\).

\item Expand the local polynomial as
\[
P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_\alpha
b_{x,\alpha}
\left(\frac{v-b_x}{r_x}\right)^\alpha .
\]
For \(h\ge 0\), define the centered factorial lift
\[
U_h(N;z)
=
\sum_{t=0}^h
\binom ht
(-z)^{h-t}
\frac{(N)_t}{m^t}.
\]

\item Define the clipping scale
\[
S_x
=
(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x},
\]
the unprojected cell estimate
\[
Z_x
=
\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
+
\sum_\alpha
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\frac{
U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})
}{
r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}
},
\]
and the clipped cell estimate
\[
T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\Pi_{
[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,
 \bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]
}
(Z_x).
\]

\item Define the randomized projected aggregate by
\[
\widetilde V
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}
\left(
\sum_{x=1}^d T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}
\right).
\]
The all-data Rao--Blackwellized estimator is
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
E\!\left[
\widetilde V
\mid
O_1,\ldots,O_n
\right],
\]
where the conditional expectation integrates only the auxiliary Poisson count \(M\) and marks \(B_1,\ldots,B_M\).
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Fixed-law squared risk
blocks.body: For an estimator \(\widehat V\) based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) and an observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), define \[ \operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}(\widehat V,\Psi):=E_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right\}^2\right], \] where \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\) denotes the law of \(n\) independent observations each distributed as \(\mathbb P\).

blocks.title: Jackson factorial risk bound
blocks.body:
Assume the sampling condition in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}: for every alphabet size \(d\), sample size \(n\), and observed finite law \(\mathbb P\), the sample law is the canonical i.i.d. product law generated by \(\mathbb P\).

Then there exist tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) such that the Jackson factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} satisfies the following guarantee whenever:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap constant \(\epsilon\) satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} The alphabet size satisfies \(d\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Observed model.)} The observed law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.
\end{itemize}
For every such \(\epsilon\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every such \(n,d\), and \(\mathbb P\),
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}
\left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}},\Psi\right)
\le
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) is the observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}.

blocks.title: \(L_1\) embedding \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\)
blocks.body:
For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), define the observed atom masses
\[
q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=\frac{P_x}{4},
\qquad
q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=\frac{Q_x}{4},
\qquad x\in[d].
\]
Complete the observed law by taking the potential outcomes to be conditionally independent Bernoulli variables, setting the treatment propensity equal to \(1/2\), and imposing consistency.

blocks.title: Fixed-sample two-sample \(L_1\) minimax risk
blocks.body: Let \((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n\) be independent paired observations with \(Z_i\sim\mathbf P\), \(W_i\sim\mathbf Q\), and \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\). The normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared error is \[ \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}:=\inf_{\widehat D}\sup_{(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2}E_{\mathbf P,\mathbf Q}\left[\left\{\widehat D((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n)-\|\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\|_1\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable real-valued functions of the paired sample.

blocks.title: Equal-propensity normalized \(L_1\) embedding
blocks.body: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), \(\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) is the full-data law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with covariate mass \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), treatment propensity \(\pi_x=1/2\), outcome regressions \(\mu_{1x}=P_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) and \(\mu_{0x}=Q_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) on cells with \(P_x+Q_x>0\), conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with these means, treatment drawn independently of the potential outcomes given \(X\), and observed outcome \(Y=Y(A)\). Equivalently, its observed margin has cell masses \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), with a consistency-compatible completion.

blocks.title: Equal-propensity L1 reduction
blocks.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(\mathbb P_0\) be an observed law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(\mu_n\) be a law on \(n\) observed triples. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The law \(\mu_n\) is the \(n\)-fold product law generated by \(\mathbb P_0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every pair \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), let
\[
\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}\{\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Obs}\) is the observed margin from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} and \(\mathrm{L1Emb}\) is the \(L_1\) embedding from \cref{obj:synth_6}. The law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, and, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2}.
\]
Moreover, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
\pi_x=\frac12,
\]
and the observed-law optimal-regression value from \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\frac12+\frac14\sum_{x\in[d]} |P_x-Q_x|.
\]
Finally, the explicit fixed-\(n\) product Markov kernel obtained by applying the single-observation \(L_1\) embedding kernel independently across the \(n\) coordinates transforms the fixed paired-sample law generated by \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) exactly into the product law \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\). Consequently, for the fixed-sample minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\frac{1}{16}\,\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon},
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\) is the normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared risk.

blocks.title: Global minimax lower bound
blocks.body:
Suppose the observed samples satisfy the independent product sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}. For every overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exists a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n\geq 1\) and \(d\geq 2\), the fixed-sample minimax squared risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
c_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

blocks.title: Matched minimax frontier
blocks.body:
There are universal tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(0<\kappa<1\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) for the Jackson factorial estimator such that the following holds.  For every fixed overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there are real constants \(c_\epsilon\) and \(C_\epsilon\) with
\[
0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon .
\]
For every \(n\geq 1\) and \(d\geq 2\), with \(L_d=\log(ed)\) and with \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) denoting the fixed-sample observed minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
c_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL_d}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
  \left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right)^2
\right]
\leq
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL_d}\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the fixed-sample minimax squared risk over the full-data causal completion class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) is exactly \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for the same \(n\), \(d\), and \(\epsilon\).

blocks.title: Causal minimax risk
blocks.body: For \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), write \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)^{\otimes n}\) for the law of \(n\) independent observations each distributed as the observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\), and define the observed-sample causal minimax squared risk by \[ \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}} E_{\operatorname{Obs}(P)^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-V^\star(P)\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\).

blocks.title: Consistency and parametric boundaries
blocks.body:
For every overlap constant \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and for every alphabet-size sequence \(d_\bullet=(d_n)_{n\ge 1}\) satisfying \(d_n\ge 2\) for all \(n\), the following equivalences hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed consistency.)} The fixed-sample minimax squared risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\longrightarrow 0
\]
if and only if
\[
d_n=o\{n\log(en)\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Causal consistency.)} The causal minimax squared risk over \(\mathcal P_{d_n,\epsilon}\) satisfies
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\longrightarrow 0
\]
if and only if
\[
d_n=o\{n\log(en)\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed parametric boundary.)} The observed minimax risk sequence has the parametric \(n^{-1}\) rate, meaning that there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\le \frac{C}{n},
\]
if and only if the alphabet-size sequence is uniformly bounded asymptotically, meaning \(d_n=O(1)\).
\item \textbf{(Causal parametric boundary.)} The causal minimax risk sequence has the parametric \(n^{-1}\) rate, meaning that there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\le \frac{C}{n},
\]
if and only if \(d_n=O(1)\).
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Tensor Jackson coefficient envelope
blocks.body:
With the Jackson kernel notation of \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}, assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(K\ge 1\) is an integer.
\item \textbf{(Function.)} \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\), where \(\mathcal J\) is the four arm-outcome coordinate set.
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \(B\ge 0\) and \(\lvert f(z)\rvert\le B\) for every \(z\in[-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a polynomial \(\mathcal R\) in the four normalized coordinates such that, for every angle vector \(\varphi:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
\mathcal R(\cos\varphi)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{\mathcal J}}
f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_K(\tau_\jmath)\,d\tau .
\]
Here cosine is applied coordinatewise. Moreover, every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)\) satisfies
\[
\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\omega\in\mathcal J,
\]
the total degree of \(\mathcal R\) is at most \(8(K-1)\), and its coefficient one-norm satisfies
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)}
\lvert \mathcal R_\beta\rvert
\le 2^{40K+20}B .
\]

blocks.title: Jackson tensor extraction
blocks.body:
Using the overlap-parameter notation of \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(K\) be an integer, and let
\(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial
\(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies
\(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for every coordinate \(\omega\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every four-coordinate vector \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right).
\]
Here \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution from
\cref{obj:def:global-extension}.
\item \textbf{(Jackson convolution.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
\]
equals the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution from \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel} of
\(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), evaluated at
\(\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}
\left|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta\right|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Tensor Jackson convolution operator $\mathcal J_K$
blocks.body: For a positive integer $K$, let $J_K(t)=c_K\{\sin(Kt/2)/\sin(t/2)\}^4$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, with the removable values filled in continuously and with $c_K$ chosen so that $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_K(t)\,dt=1$. For a finite coordinate dimension $D$ and a function $f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R$, the order-$K$ tensor Jackson convolution is the operator $\mathcal J_K$ defined, for $\theta\in\mathbb R^D$, by \[ (\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\theta) := \int_{[-\pi,\pi]^D} f\{\cos(\theta+t)\}\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)\,dt, \] where cosine and addition are coordinatewise. Equivalently, the product kernel $\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)$ is normalized to have integral one over $[-\pi,\pi]^D$.

blocks.title: Tensor Jackson modulus
blocks.body:
Let \(D\) be a finite coordinate dimension, let \(K\) be a positive integer, and let \(f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R\). Let \(L\ge0\), let \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i\ge0\) for each \(i\in[D]\), and fix an angle vector \(\varphi\in\mathbb R^D\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Kernel.)} The order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution is formed from the order-four Jackson kernel in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}.
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The function \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^D\).
\item \textbf{(Weighted increment modulus.)} For every shift \(\tau\in\mathbb R^D\),
\[
\left|f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(a_i|\tau_i|+b_i\tau_i^2\right),
\]
where cosine is applied coordinatewise.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|(\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\varphi)-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(\frac{32a_i}{K}+\frac{64b_i}{K^2}\right).
\]

blocks.title: Simultaneous Jackson certificate
blocks.body:
There is a universal constant \(A>0\) such that, for every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) with the following property. Let:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Rectangle.)} \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) have \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\), and positive radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}>0
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(P_{x,K}\) be the tensor Jackson polynomial associated with \(\epsilon\), \(K\), and \(Q_x\) in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. Then the same polynomial satisfies all of the following conclusions:
\[
\deg_{\jmath}(P_{x,K})\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
For every \(v\in Q_x\),
\[
\left|P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{
\frac{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}}{K}
+
\frac{r_{\jmath,x}}{K^2}
\right\}.
\]
There are a finite multi-index set \(\mathcal A_x\) and coefficients \(b_{x,\alpha}\) such that, for every \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left(\frac{v_{\jmath}-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right)^{\alpha_{\jmath}},
\]
with
\[
\alpha_{\jmath}\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\text{ and every }\jmath\in\mathcal J,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
A^K(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]

blocks.title: Bad pilot moment bound
blocks.body:
Fix the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\). Let \(q=(q_\jmath)_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\) have nonnegative coordinates, let \(m>0\), let \(L\ge 1\), and let \(t\in\{1,2,4\}\). Suppose the pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\) are independent with
\[
N'_{\jmath}\sim \operatorname{Pois}(m q_\jmath),
\qquad \jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
With \(H_0=1024\), define the normalized aggregate pilot score
\[
\Gamma(N')
=
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left[
\left|{N'_{\jmath}\over m}-q_\jmath\right|
+
H_0\left\{\sqrt{{N'_{\jmath}\over m}{L\over m}}+{L\over m}\right\}
\right],
\]
and define the self-normalized bad-pilot event
\[
\mathsf G^c
=
\left\{
\exists\,\jmath\in\mathcal J:
\left|{N'_{\jmath}\over m}-q_\jmath\right|
>
{H_0\over 4}
\left\{\sqrt{{N'_{\jmath}\over m}{L\over m}}+{L\over m}\right\}
\right\}.
\]
Then, with \(C_t=10^{80(t+1)}\),
\[
E\!\left[\Gamma(N')^t\mathbf 1_{\mathsf G^c}\right]
\le
C_t e^{-20L}
\left\{
\sqrt{{\left(\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\right)L\over m}}
+
{L\over m}
\right\}^{t}.
\]

blocks.title: Good-pilot event
blocks.body: Fix a cell \(x\), four-cell mass vector \(q_x=(q_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), alphabet logarithm \(L_d=\log(ed)\), pilot-radius constant \(H_0\), and pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\). Put \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\) and \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\). The coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle is \[\mathsf G_x:=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\left\{\left|\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m}-q_{\jmath,x}\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\}.\]

blocks.title: Good pilot radius bound
blocks.body:
Fix \(m>0\), an integer \(d\ge 1\), pilot counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) for \(\jmath\) in the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J\), and coordinate intensities \(q_\jmath\ge 0\).  Let \(L_d=\log(ed)\), set \(p_x=\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\), and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be the canonical pilot rectangle of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}, with radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume that the good-pilot event
\[
\mathsf G_x=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{\left|c_{\jmath,x}-q_\jmath\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\},
\qquad c_{\jmath,x}=\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m},
\]
holds, where \(h_{\jmath,x}\) is the canonical pilot half-width in \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}.  Then
\[
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}
\le
2\cdot 10^6
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x L_d}{m}}+\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Normalized coefficient envelope
blocks.body:
Let \(\epsilon>0\) be the overlap parameter from \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a rectangle over the four outcome-arm coordinate set \(\mathcal J\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Ordered endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} With
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\]
one has \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(b_x=(b_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), let \(r_x=(r_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), and let \(P_{x,K}\) be the Jackson tensor polynomial attached to \(Q_x\) by \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. Define
\[
\mathcal R_{x,K}(z)
=
P_{x,K}\bigl((b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}z_\jmath)_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\bigr)
-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x} b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} z_\jmath^{\alpha_\jmath},
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cell extension from \cref{obj:def:global-extension} and \(\mathcal A_x=\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\). Then
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
(2^{60})^{K}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
Moreover, every \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\) satisfies
\[
\alpha_\jmath\le 2(K-1)
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

blocks.title: Pilot-failure contributions
blocks.body: Fix a cell \(x\), a four-cell mass vector \(q_x\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), and Jackson tuning. Let \(\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}\) denote the product-Poisson law of the pilot and evaluation count vectors, and let \(\mathsf G_x\) be the coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle in the Jackson--factorial construction. With \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\) denoting the clipped cell statistic built from the pilot and evaluation counts, define \[ \mathrm{PF}_{1,x}:=\int_{\mathsf G_x^c}\left|T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\right|\,d\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}, \qquad \mathrm{PF}_{2,x}:=\int_{\mathsf G_x^c}\left(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\right)^2\,d\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}. \]

blocks.title: Centered factorial pilot control
blocks.body:
Assume the product experiment satisfies the i.i.d. sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.  There is a universal Jackson tuning with self-normalized Poisson pilot-radius constant, polynomial-degree constant \(\kappa=1/100000\), and cutoff \(D_0=3\).  For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that the following assertions hold for every \(n,d\), every observed law \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every positive sample size \(n\), whenever \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.  Set \(m=n/8\), let \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) be the four-coordinate cell vector, and let \(p_x\) be the marginal mass of cell \(x\).

In the uncapped marked experiment generated by
\[
M\sim \operatorname{Pois}(n/4)
\]
together with i.i.d. observations from \(\mathbb P\) and independent fair pilot/evaluation marks, the count \(M\) has law \(\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\).  The induced pilot/evaluation table has law equal to the product, over cells \(x\in[d]\) and coordinates \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), of two independent Poisson count arrays with coordinate means \(m q_{\jmath,x}\).  For each fixed cell \(x\), the marginal law of the pilot and evaluation counts in that cell is therefore
\[
\bigotimes_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\jmath,x})
\otimes
\bigotimes_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\jmath,x}).
\]

For every cell \(x\), every fixed pilot table, every coordinate \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), every \(z\in\mathbb R\), and every \(h,t\in\mathbb N\), conditional expectation over the evaluation counts satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[U_h(N_{\jmath,x};z)\mid N'\right]
=
(q_{\jmath,x}-z)^h
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[U_h(N_{\jmath,x};z)U_t(N_{\jmath,x};z)\mid N'\right]
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{h,t\}}
\binom{h}{\ell}\binom{t}{\ell}\ell!
\left(\frac{q_{\jmath,x}}{m}\right)^\ell
(q_{\jmath,x}-z)^{h+t-2\ell}.
\]

With the same tuning, the clipped Jackson-factorial cell statistic \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\) obeys, uniformly over all cells \(x\in[d]\),
\[
\left|
\mathbb E T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)
\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac{1}{mL_d}
\right\},
\]
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})
\le
C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
\left\{
\frac{p_x L_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}
\right\},
\]
and the pilot-failure contributions satisfy
\[
\mathrm{PF}_{1,x}
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac{1}{mL_d}
\right\},
\qquad
\mathrm{PF}_{2,x}
\le
C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
\left\{
\frac{p_x L_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Poisson minimax risk
Dense contrast law
blocks.body:
For an integer \(d\geq 2\) and a contrast vector \(\theta=(\theta_x)_{x\in[d]}\) with \(\theta_x\in[-1/2,1/2]\) for every \(x\in[d]\), define \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) as the full-data probability law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) whose atom at \((x,a,y,y_0,y_1)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^4\) is
\[
P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}(x,a,y,y_0,y_1)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{2d}\, b_{(1-\theta_x)/2}(y_0)\, b_{(1+\theta_x)/2}(y_1),
& y=y_a,\\[0.8em]
0,
& y\neq y_a,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(y_a=y_1\) if \(a=1\) and \(y_a=y_0\) if \(a=0\), and \(b_\mu(1)=\mu\), \(b_\mu(0)=1-\mu\).

blocks.title: Dense moment-matching construction
blocks.body:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), the overlap parameter, a dense domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon,\qquad
\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) indexed by positive even degrees, define the dense moment-matching construction as follows.  For every positive even \(K\), the family carries the prior-pair conditions that \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) are probability measures supported on \([-1,1]\), are symmetric, have matching moments through degree \(K\), and satisfy
\[
\int_{-1}^1 |t|\,d\nu_{1,K}(t)
-
\int_{-1}^1 |t|\,d\nu_{0,K}(t)
=
2E_K .
\]
The construction has components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense law.)} For each \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome law induced by the dense full-data masses, equivalently \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), and \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), with \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables given \(X=x\), \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and \(Y=Y(A)\).
\item \textbf{(Approximation scale.)} The approximation degree and best even-degree approximation error are
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_d\rceil,
\qquad
E_K=\inf\left\{e\in\mathbb R:\exists p,\ \deg(p)\le K,\ 
\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e\right\}.
\]
The construction uses \(E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\).
\item \textbf{(Poisson intensity and amplitude.)} The one-cell Poisson intensity and dense contrast amplitude are
\[
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},
\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate priors.)} The coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\qquad
\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense product priors.)} The priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are the pushforwards into the dense contrast class of the restrictions of \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) and \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) to \([-1,1]^d\), under coordinatewise scaling by \(a_{n,d}\).
\item \textbf{(Observation mixtures.)} The mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) are the observation-kernel mixtures induced by \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with independent Poissonized sample size \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).
\item \textbf{(Risk and separation.)} The risk component is the Poissonized minimax risk
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}.
\]
The prior target-mean separation is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
The construction carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},
\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

blocks.title: Dense amplitude range
blocks.body:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(2\le d\) and \(d^2<n\). For the lower-bound contrast amplitude \(a_{n,d}\) defined in \cref{obj:def:dense-moment-matching-construction},
\[
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12.
\]

blocks.title: Total variation distance
blocks.body: For probability laws \(\mathbb M_0\) and \(\mathbb M_1\) on a common measurable space, define \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_0,\mathbb M_1)=\sup_{B}\lvert \mathbb M_0(B)-\mathbb M_1(B)\rvert\), where the supremum ranges over measurable events \(B\).

blocks.title: Dense likelihood tail
blocks.body: For the dense lower-bound degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\), Poissonized cell intensity \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and dense amplitude \(a_{n,d}\), define the dense likelihood tail by \[\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}:=\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}.\]

blocks.title: One-cell dense likelihood ratio
blocks.body: Fix a Poisson cell intensity \(\lambda\ge0\). Let \(R_+\) and \(R_-\) be the two sign counts in one dense cell, and let \(E_0\) denote expectation under the zero-contrast baseline law \(R_+,R_-\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda/2)\). For \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), the one-cell likelihood ratio relative to this baseline is \[ L_\theta(R_+,R_-):=(1+\theta)^{R_+}(1-\theta)^{R_-}. \] In the dense lower bound, \(L_{\theta_x}\) applies this definition with the cell contrast \(\theta_x\) and \(\lambda=\lambda_{n,d}\).

blocks.title: Dense moment matching lower bound
blocks.body:
Suppose the product experiment satisfies the i.i.d. sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.  There is an integer cutoff \(D_0\geq2\) such that, for every overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there is a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) with the following property.  For all integers \(d,n\) satisfying \(d\geq D_0\) and \(d^2<n\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree and amplitude.)} The lower-bound degree and amplitude obey
\[
8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2,
\qquad
a_{n,d}^2=\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d}{128n},
\qquad
a_{n,d}\leq \frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense observed submodel.)} For every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), the dense equal-mass contrast submodel \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) has observed margin in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and satisfies, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac1d,
\qquad
\pi_x=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1x}=\frac{1+\theta_x}{2},
\qquad
\mu_{0x}=\frac{1-\theta_x}{2},
\]
with
\[
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
=
\frac12+\frac{1}{2d}\sum_{x=1}^d|\theta_x|.
\]
\item \textbf{(Moment-matched priors and mixtures.)} The two dense product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with induced Poissonized mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\), may be chosen so that their prior-mean separation satisfies
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\qquad
0<\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\leq1,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
\leq
d\{\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\}^{1/2}
\leq
d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}
\leq\frac1{16}.
\]
Under each of the two product priors, the target is concentrated around its prior mean:
\[
\int
\left(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-\mathbb E_{\Pi_{j,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\right)^2
\,d\Pi_{j,n,d}(\theta)
\leq
\frac{a_{n,d}^2}{4d},
\qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
and
\[
\Pi_{j,n,d}\left(
\left|\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-\mathbb E_{\Pi_{j,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\right|
>
\frac{\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}}{4}
\right)
\leq
\frac18,
\qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(One-cell likelihood identity.)} For all contrasts \(\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_0[L_\theta L_{\theta'}]
=
\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta\theta').
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently,
\[
c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2
\leq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\qquad
c_\epsilon\frac{d}{nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}
\leq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\]
and the fixed-sample and Poissonized risks satisfy
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\geq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}
-
\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}.
\]
In particular,
\[
c_\epsilon\frac{d}{nL_d}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]
